title: Joined is not the same as reachable
hook: Pages link one way. How many can you actually click your way to?

knows: web pages link to other pages
what reaching a page by following links means
doesNotKnow: that links are one-way, so being connected is not the same as being reachable
the bow-tie shape of the web

misconception: If two pages are joined by links somewhere, you can click from one to the other. The web is one big connected thing.
objective: The learner can explain that because links are one-way, the pages you can click to from a start page are fewer than the pages joined to it: from a core page you reach the core and OUT pages but never IN, and from an OUT page almost nowhere.

claims.text: In the 12-page graph on the stage, following links the way they point reaches 7 pages from each of A, B, C and D (counting the start), 10 from E, 8 from F, 3 from G, 2 from H, 1 from I, 1 from J, 2 from K and 1 from L. The reveal quotes only the pages the learner tapped.
claims.source: Node BFS over the exact edge list in Demo.tsx: A>B, B>C, C>D, D>A, D>B, C>G, D>H, E>A, E>F, E>J, F>B, G>H, H>I, K>L. Builder ran it 2026-10-14 (reach(start) as in Demo.tsx); output {A:7,B:7,C:7,D:7,E:10,F:8,G:3,H:2,I:1,J:1,K:2,L:1}. Deterministic, no seed. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass NCM-1): Own BFS over the 14-edge list copied from Demo.tsx (scratchpad fc/bow.mjs): {A:7,B:7,C:7,D:7,E:10,F:8,G:3,H:2,I:1,J:1,K:2,L:1}. Reveal computes reach(p).size for the first page tapped in each group; "From p only itself" only for size 1 (I, J, L not in core/in/out groups except I). Matches.

claims.text: Ignoring link direction, 10 of the 12 pages are joined to A (all but K and L).
claims.source: Node BFS over the same edge list treated as undirected from A: component = A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I, J (10 pages); K and L form their own pair. Builder ran it 2026-10-14. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass NCM-1): Own undirected BFS from A: ABCDEFGHIJ (10); K-L a separate pair. Predict text "10 of them are joined to the central group" matches.

claims.text: Links point one way, so being joined is not the same as being reachable: from the middle group (A to D) you can click out to G, H and I, but no link leads back to E or F.
claims.source: Definition of a directed link plus the edge list in c1: reach(A) = A, B, C, D, G, H, I, which contains neither E nor F; A, B, C, D reach each other (checked in node). Holds for this graph. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass NCM-1): reach(A)=reach(B)=reach(C)=reach(D)=ABCDGHI; pages that reach A are only A-F; no edge enters E or F from A-D. Reveal wording (middle -> right, nothing back to the left, right end leads almost nowhere: G 3, H 2, I 1) matches the stage.

claims.text: The real web has a bow-tie shape: a tightly linked core, pages that lead into it, pages it leads out to, and a few detached pieces.
claims.source: Broder, Kumar, Maghoul, Raghavan, Rajagopalan, Stata, Tomkins and Wiener, 'Graph structure in the Web', Computer Networks 33 (2000); Easley and Kleinberg, Networks, Crowds, and Markets (2010), ch. 13. NEEDS A HUMAN SOURCE CHECK (builder cited from the brief and memory; no access to the paper). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass NCM-1): Broder et al. abstract and secondary summaries (search, 2026-10-14; primary PDF unreachable through the proxy) describe the bow-tie: strongly connected core (about 28%), IN, OUT, plus tendrils and disconnected components. E&K ch. 13 is the structure-of-the-Web chapter (library catalogue records); section stays unconfirmed. Advisory: the reveal omits tendrils and "a few detached pieces" understates the disconnected part; not false.

claims.text: Broder and colleagues (2000) mapped about 200 million pages.
claims.source: Broder et al. 2000 (crawl of about 203 million pages, from the brief and the review record). NEEDS A HUMAN SOURCE CHECK. The core and IN/OUT percentages (about 28%, 21%, 21%) in the brief are deliberately NOT shown to learners; add them only after the paper is checked. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass NCM-1): Abstract as quoted in search results: "two AltaVista crawls each with over 200 million pages and 1.5 billion links"; Nature news (2000) "analysed 200 million web pages". "About 200 million" holds. The 28/21/21% figures remain unshown; core about 28% corroborated by secondary sources only.

claims.text: This 12-page graph is a toy, not to scale.
claims.source: Disclosure that the stage is a teaching model, not data from the crawl. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass NCM-1): Disclosure is present in the reveal ("This 12-page graph is a toy, not to scale").

claims.text: Extra check, not shown to learners: over the 132 ordered pairs of distinct pages in the toy graph, 44 have a click path (one third).
claims.source: Node: sum of (reach(start) - 1) over the 12 starts = 44 of 12*11 = 132. Builder ran it 2026-10-14. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass NCM-1): Own script: sum of (reach-1) = 44 of 132 ordered pairs.

recall.question: Page X links to page Y, but Y has no link back to X, and nothing else links to X. Starting on Y, can you click your way to X?
options: Yes: they are joined by a link
No: links only work in the direction they point
Only if you go through a third page
recall.why: Links are one-way, so being joined is not the same as being reachable. Y has no link out that leads back to X.

references.note: bow-tie structure of the web; section unconfirmed (brief says 13.3-13.4)
